mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-11.6 to -22.9), indicating a persistent avoidance trend driven by ongoing case-surge caution; this momentum is expected to carry forward, producing a further mean decline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weeks of decline in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite the prior four-week monotonic decline, falsifying pure momentum persistence.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation of RESIDENTIAL above 12 points for two consecutive weeks signals entrenched stay-at-home behavior (self-isolation, risk aversion) that substitutes for retail outings, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 12 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 13.4 and 14.1 in t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains above 12 points, rejecting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Deep and simultaneous suppression of TRANSIT (around -56) and WORKPLACES (fluctuating -32 to -59) jointly removes the commuting-linked foot traffic that typically feeds retail and recreation visits; the combined effect compounds to push RETAIL_REC lower than either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT below -48 and WORKPLACES below -32 in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even as both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply negative, indicating no compounding commute-linked suppression.

mechanism_narrative: The current snapshot reflects peak Omicron-wave case-surge policy caution (deep TRANSIT and WORKPLACES troughs); once this policy/behavioral regime passes its peak, pent-up demand drives a rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as restrictions and voluntary avoidance ease.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES recovers more than 10 points week-on-week after prior sharp decline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded from -59.0 to -32.0 between t-2w and t-0w
regime_hint: Omicron wave peak passing / reopening transition
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days despite a clear rebound in WORKPLACES, rejecting the peak-passing rebound mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: January in NSW is the peak summer holiday period; as the holiday season ends and schools/offices resume in late January, typical seasonal mobility patterns normalize, driving an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks independent of case-surge dynamics.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2022-01-15 falls within Australian summer holiday period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even as the calendar moves past the typical end-of-holiday period in late January, rejecting the seasonal normalization mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in GROCERY_PHARM (10.7 to 1.9) indicates that earlier panic/pantry-stocking behavior is fading without being replaced by discretionary retail activity, implying broad consumer caution persists and RETAIL_REC continues to weaken over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 10.7 to 1.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM, rejecting the shared-caution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls below -55 for two consecutive weeks (a threshold consistent with active government advisories or capacity restrictions on public transport), this signals an intensified policy-driven mobility clampdown that will further depress RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -55 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -56.4 in t-2w and t-1w and -55.9 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following two consecutive weeks of TRANSIT below -55, rejecting the policy-clampdown threshold mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising RESIDENTIAL and volatile PARKS mobility (swinging between -8.9 and 21.6) suggests outdoor summer leisure activity is substituting for indoor retail visits; as summer heat and holiday outdoor use wane in coming weeks, this substitution effect reverses, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -5.3 to 21.6 to 3.4 to -8.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days even as PARKS mobility stabilizes and RESIDENTIAL mobility falls, rejecting the outdoor-substitution reversal mechanism.
